title: Introduce TFState consistency signer and rolling GPU pool migrator
author: Priya Nair
release_notes:
- Added tfstate-consistency-signer module to certify state snapshots.
- Added rolling GPU pool migrator module to move workloads with zero-downtime.
- Backwards-compatible; no action required for most customers. See migration notes.
description:
Context: Private deployments have started seeing occasional tfstate divergence when a parallel apply overlaps subnet and GPU nodepool changes. This caused transient resource duplication and occasional evictions in large clusters. This PR introduces two complementary Terraform modules and operational tooling: a tfstate-consistency-signer (lightweight helper that writes a signed checkpoint blob to a central state bucket after coordinated applies) and a rolling-gpu-pool-migrator (controller-like module that emits an ordered plan to rotate GPU nodepools across AZs with minimal disruption).

What this PR does:
- New module: modules/tfstate-consistency-signer
  - Generates a signed metadata file (s3/gs) that includes apply-id, timestamp, and checksum of the state file.
  - Integrates with existing state backend configuration via optional provider hooks; does NOT replace backend.
  - Includes an optional pre-apply validation step (terraform null_resource + local-exec) to fail fast if signatures mismatch.
- New module: modules/rolling-gpu-pool-migrator
  - Accepts current nodepool map, target nodepool spec, and a rotation window policy.
  - Produces a plan file (JSON) listing atomic steps (drain -> cordon -> create -> attach -> validate -> destroy) that operators can review.
  - Supports canary rotation and health-check gating (kube-probe based) for on-prem and VPC installs.
- Changes to examples/ and docs/ showing upgrade workflow and recommended Linear ticket template.

Migration plan (operators):
1) Deploy tfstate-consistency-signer as an opt-in module referencing existing state bucket.
2) Run a single coordinated apply (signer will write checkpoint blob). Verify signed checksum in bucket and compare to current state.
3) Enable rolling-gpu-pool-migrator in dry-run to emit plan and review.
4) Execute rotation with canary=1, monitor console dashboards, then increase batch size.

Rollback and safety:
- All changes are additive; signer is opt-in and migrator supports dry-run.
- In case of partial rotation failure, migrator emits rollback steps and preserves the old nodepool for fast reattach.
- The pre-apply signer validation will block automated CI applies if detected checksum mismatch, reducing merge-time conflicts.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for signer HMAC generation and plan serializer (modules/tests)
- Integration tests using minikube + local S3 mock to verify plan execution and node drain/reattach flows (ci/integration)
- Load tests on staging clusters to simulate concurrent terraform applies and verify signer prevents divergent state

Related work: ENG-2211 (state incident post-release), ENG-2247 (gpu-allocator drift detector), SUP-1198 (customer report for on-prem eviction during upgrade).

Checklist:
- [x] modules implemented
- [x] docs and examples updated
- [x] tests added and passing in CI
- [x] migration and rollback guidance included

Notes: This PR purposely keeps the signer as a small helper (no secret management baked-in beyond HMAC key); we'll follow up with KMS/HSM integration and a controller-based signer if adoption metrics justify it.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Nice approach—can you clarify the HMAC key rotation story? If the key rotates, how do we validate older checkpoints? Author reply: The signer writes key_id along with HMAC and we keep a key history map in the state bucket. Rotation is handled by adding new key entries; the validation code accepts previous keys for N days (configurable), docs updated.

Sofia Martinez: Migrator plan appears to assume that CSI volumes can be reattached quickly. On some on-prem infra that is not true. Suggest adding configurable drain timeout and force-retire flags. Author reply: Added drain_timeout and force_retire variables; default conservative values included and documented.

Liam O'Connor: CI integration failed on first run due to localstack S3 pathing. Request: add retry logic and clearer errors. Author reply: Fixed localstack path handling and added exponential backoff for uploads.

QA Bot: Integration tests passed in dry-run but failed in execution for a specific scenario where node labels didn't match filter. Author reply: Updated migrator filters to accept label selectors and fallback to taints when labels missing; added test coverage.
merge_outcome: merged after approvals and CI green
notes: operator-facing docs include example kubectl commands for on-prem reattach; watchlist: monitor node eviction rate for 24h after rotation
